clue.text: Room for Germans in 1811?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: the frame named after this word is found in an old people's home

blocks.note: first meaning: the German word for a room
second meaning: the walking frame found in an old people's home (18 and 11)

explanation.surface: A question about accommodation for German visitors in the year 1811.
explanation.walkthrough: 1811 looks like a year, but it is the cross-references 18 and 11, OLD PEOPLE'S HOME. A Zimmer frame is a walking aid, and Zimmer is German for room.
explanation.definitionFit: Zimmer is the ordinary German noun for a room, and also the trade name of a metal walking frame.

clue.text: Shot on target and the Frenchman will croak

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the creature that does it

blocks.note: a shot in the centre of a target is a bull, short for bull's-eye
Frog is old British slang for a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A marksman scores a bull's-eye and the French victim will die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Croak' looks like slang for dying, which suits the shooting; it is the noise of the big amphibian.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullfrog is a large frog famous for its loud, deep croaking call.

clue.text: Act dumb initially with stone hitting bumper

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word dumb only

blocks.note: to do is to act
its first letter
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A silent actor is struck by a thrown stone, which bumps into them.
explanation.walkthrough: A dodgem is a fairground bumper car, built to bash into the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgems are the small electric fairground cars also called bumper cars, made for colliding.

clue.text: Fruit painter is at home

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock painter
taken as written
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: An artist sits at home with a bowl of fruit, perhaps painting a still life.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a dried grape, so it is one kind of fruit eaten as a snack or baked.

clue.text: Area of flower country given a lift without oxygen

without in its old sense of outside, so one part goes round the other

explanation.surface: A country of flowers is airlifted somewhere with no oxygen, like a nursery shipment to space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's river; the Niger names a river and the country it runs through.
explanation.definitionFit: A region is a district or tract of land, so it is a general word for an area.

clue.text: Marine mammal moved soil on string

blocks.note: to dig is to move soil, and dug is its past tense
taken as written
G is a violin string, as in the G-string

explanation.surface: Someone digs earth while fiddling with a piece of string, an odd scene of gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: The dugong is a large plant-eating sea creature related to the manatee, sometimes called the sea cow.

clue.text: Hunting, shooting, or fishing, say, in larger understanding

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the next words of the clue

blocks.note: the end of larger and the start of understanding

explanation.surface: Country sports, the clue suggests, give a person a broader grasp of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a list of country pursuits; grammatically each is a verb form ending in -ing used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunting, shooting and fishing are each examples of a verbal noun, an -ing form doing a noun's work.

clue.text: Second Labour premier absorbing fluid with alien armada

indicators.note: a premier absorbing something takes it into himself, so it goes inside his name

blocks.note: B is second, as a B grade is second class
Clement Attlee, Labour prime minister 1945-51
FL is the abbreviation for fluid
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A runner-up Labour leader takes in drink alongside a fleet of invading spaceships.
explanation.walkthrough: Attlee was Britain's first Labour prime minister with a majority, after Churchill in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships assembled for battle, as with the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: What's responsible for images of 20 1?

indicators.note: what is responsible for a word has produced it, so the answer is made from that word rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as the fodder

explanation.surface: A question about who shapes the stereotyped pictures of the elderly in the media.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines, and 'images' rearranged supplies the letters; 20 1 is SENIOR CITIZENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice against the elderly is what produces demeaning stereotyped portrayals of pensioners.

clue.text: Moral tale has the bloody lot on ecstasy

blocks.note: goes with lot: the lot is everything
the lot is everything, all of it
E is the street name for the drug ecstasy
gory means covered in blood

explanation.surface: A cautionary story full of blood and drugs, the whole gang high on ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the lot before the drug; the bloody part follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story with a hidden symbolic meaning, often teaching a moral lesson.

clue.text: See 18

explanation.definitionFit: Together with the light at 18 it names a residential institution where elderly people live and are cared for.

clue.text: 18 (11) needs payment to take in weary setter

definitions.note: the clue asks for a word that, put before the light at 11, names an old people's home

the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.definitionFit: A retirement home is a residence for elderly people who have stopped working, an old people's home.

clue.text: 10's upset about time at the pictures for 11 dealer

explanation.definitionFit: 11 is HOME, and an estate agent is the British name for a realtor, who deals in houses.

clue.text: A cat is presented to the Queen to make little drops

definitions.note: a purpose phrase standing for the device that serves it

blocks.note: taken as written
a tom is a male cat
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at a pet's droppings; the drops are fine spray.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid such as perfume into a fine spray of tiny droplets.

clue.text: Modern culture retaining spelling in principal part of paper

indicators.note: a culture retaining something keeps it held within itself

blocks.note: New Age is the modern alternative culture of crystals and mysticism
sp is the proofreader's abbreviation for spelling

explanation.surface: Modern culture keeps its spelling inside the main part of the newspaper, a gripe about standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spelling' looks like a topic for the paper; it is just the abbreviation SP.
explanation.definitionFit: The news pages carry the main reporting of a newspaper, as opposed to sport, features or adverts.

clue.text: Frank's garments, half of the sixes

VI is six in Roman numerals, so sixes are VIs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name; it is a member of the Germanic Franks, whose king Clovis founded France.
explanation.definitionFit: Clovis I was the first king of the Franks around AD 500, so he was a Frank.

clue.text: Famous death in the engine?

blocks.note: surface: a celebrated demise, read as a large or notable ending
setter's reading: the part of a motor where a connecting rod meets the crankshaft

explanation.walkthrough: A big end is a large ending, so a famous death; it is also the end of a connecting rod in a car engine, whose failure is costly.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piston engine the big end is the larger end of the connecting rod, attached to the crankshaft.

clue.text: Old stick of a lawyer by whom Margaret's granny's embraced

clue.text: (and 1) Sincere Zionist settled maybe with pensions

clue.text: (and 25) 20 1 in 11s don't quite emulate Beckett characters

clue.text: 18 (11) has poles covered in fat
